editorial:
Ever wonder how the Catholic Mass changed so much in just a few years? You get a front-row seat to the drama behind the scenes of Vatican II. The story focuses on Annibale Bugnini, the man who drove the changes, and the brave people who tried to stop him. It feels less like a dry history lesson and more like a political thriller. You will see how a few powerful people made decisions that affected millions of believers, and you will feel the tension as they argued over the very heart of their faith.

What really works here is the way the documentary uses old records and interviews to build a mystery. The pacing is steady, and it keeps you curious about what the Pope was actually thinking. While it takes a strong stance on the issue, it provides plenty of evidence to keep you engaged. If you enjoy deep dives into secret meetings and power struggles, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by showing the long-term fallout of the new Mass. You see how the changes created a deep split in the Church that still exists today. The final scenes explain that while the New Mass became the standard, the fight to keep the old Tridentine Mass never truly died. It ends with a reflection on how the push for modernization might have cost the Church its sense of timeless tradition.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves church history or political mysteries.
